registration_status: Versioned engineering design, not externally timestamped research preregistration
participants: Independent Python authority and receiver child processes, separate SQLite databases and key files, with a trusted fixture operator on the same host
data: Synthetic owned SQLite record writes only; ephemeral authentication/signing keys are never bundled in public evidence

scenario_oracles.positive: A current exact grant commits one actual receiver record and an authenticated receipt settles one external reservation.
scenario_oracles.stop_restore: Snapshot the local receiver, acknowledge external STOP, restore the snapshot while the receiver is stopped, then restart the identical pinned receiver. A previously current grant has zero new acceptance and zero new record effects.
scenario_oracles.terminal_restore: Commit one actual record, restore the local snapshot that predates it while external authority remains ACTIVE, then submit the identical action. The surviving external terminal entry prevents a new execution even though the local effect inventory was rolled back.
scenario_oracles.pending_duplicate: A real externally issued permit with no definitive receiver outcome remains unresolved. A duplicate request does not obtain an executable permit or write a record, and STOP remains STOP_PENDING rather than falsely acknowledging STOPPED.
scenario_oracles.authority_restart: Restart the authority with its existing database and keys, without initialization. Its public pin and stopped root remain unchanged; a stale grant has zero effects.
scenario_oracles.authority_outage: Stop the authority process while the receiver remains live. A fresh request produces no receiver acceptance and no record effect. Restoring the same authority permits an unrelated fresh positive control.
scenario_oracles.split_api_denied: The externally governed receiver rejects separate accept/finalize entry points without a record effect.
scenario_oracles.unsafe_local_restore: The explicitly labeled existing local-only governed baseline accepts one old grant after its own STOP state is rolled back. A non-executing unsafe baseline invalidates this comparison.

measurement: Collect actual HTTP receiver receipts, complete receiver record inventories, signed external authority responses, and controller-signed checkpoint entries. Bind source commit/tree/dirty state and actual input-file SHA-256 digests.
rollback_method: Use SQLite backup into and out of a separate snapshot file with the receiver child process stopped. The authority process and its separate database are not rolled back.
collection_barrier: Every HTTP request completes or explicitly fails; each child process is terminated and reaped. Unknown outcomes cannot be interpreted as definitive zero-effect recovery.
revocation_boundary: STOP_PENDING closes admission; STOPPED additionally means all previously issued permits are terminal. Preaccepted work may finish; STOP is not rollback.
evidence_authentication: Authority responses/checkpoints use a pinned Ed25519 public key. Receiver receipts use a separate HMAC key retained outside public evidence; public receipt authenticity is not claimed.
scope_limits: Trusted host, fixture operator, receiver code, controller database, signing key and clock
Local database rollback only, not malicious receiver memory restoration
Record target only; no general network/tool/kernel containment
No protection against rollback of the separately trusted authority database itself without an independent latest anchor
No live-model, model-honesty or emergent swarm result
statistics: One fixed engineering scenario per case, not a population safety estimate. Do not pool with previous unit, Docker or model evaluations.
